description:
Removes the two `fatalError("unimplemented")` landmines left standing by `30`.

**`writeRemainder` (`StorageGovernor.swift:62`)** is the resume path — `TUSKitTransport:73` calls it whenever offset > 0. The existing TODO already names the design: *FileHandle seek + chunked read/write, re-sampling pressure every N MB*. That re-sampling is the point: free space is not a constant, and the original bug this whole project exists to retire was iOS reclaiming the app's cache mid-transfer.

**PHAsset export (`StorageGovernor.swift:91`)** is the one source that genuinely cannot be seeked, so it is the one case where the *no chunk temp files* commitment yields and a staged copy is written — which is exactly when a storage reservation matters.

Hold the line on the design commitment: a staging copy here is the documented exception, not permission to stage elsewhere.

userStories.title: `writeRemainder` streams from the source and re-samples pressure
userStories.description: Seek and chunked copy, with free-space re-sampled as it goes so a reclamation mid-write is caught.
acceptanceCriteria: `writeRemainder` is implemented; no `fatalError` remains on that path.
It streams byte ranges from the source without materialising a full copy.
Free space is re-sampled during the write, and a mid-write shortfall aborts cleanly with a typed error rather than a partial file left behind.
A test simulates free space collapsing mid-write and asserts the abort path and the cleanup.
userStories.notes: swift build and .chief/verify.sh green; AmphoraPathTests reported 44 passed, including offset streaming and mid-write pressureRose cleanup.

userStories.title: PHAsset export writes a staged copy under a reservation
userStories.description: The documented exception to no-chunk-temp-files, and the only place a reservation gates a copy.
acceptanceCriteria: PHAsset export is implemented via `PHAssetResourceManager`, no `fatalError` remains.
The export happens under a storage reservation; a denied reservation fails the job with a typed error rather than proceeding.
The staged copy is removed on completion, cancel AND failure — asserted for all three.
A test covers a PHAsset source end to end against a transport double.
userStories.notes: ./.chief/verify.sh green: Swift build, Swift path tests 44 passed, and TypeScript typecheck passed; PHAsset export now uses PHAssetResourceManager under a reservation with failure cleanup and state-machine completion/cancel cleanup.
